ui.agentMessages.dialog.title.tone: sentence case, product name kept as-is
ui.agentMessages.dialog.title.length: Short heading; one line at the shipped dialog width.
ui.agentMessages.dialog.title.note: Names the feature and the product it belongs to. "Radient" is the organization product name — never translate. This dialog appears once per account and tenant; the heading is the first thing it says.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.lead.tone: plain, second person, no marketing claims
ui.agentMessages.dialog.lead.length: One sentence; may wrap to two lines.
ui.agentMessages.dialog.lead.note: Explains the core offer: the user's agent can exchange messages with other members' agents inside the organization. "Agent" here is the product's agent noun; keep it consistent with the rest of the app.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.reach.length: One sentence naming the Settings path; keep "Settings → Agent messages" recognizable.
ui.agentMessages.dialog.reach.note: States the safe default (organization members only) and where to change it. The Settings → Agent messages path is a UI location the user must be able to find in their own locale — translate the "Settings" and "Agent messages" words only if those surfaces translate them.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.later.role: quiet helper under the dialog actions
ui.agentMessages.dialog.later.note: Tells the user enabling can wait; it is the polite dismissal path's companion, not a second button. Must not read as a warning.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.activities.role: capability list item inside the dialog
ui.agentMessages.dialog.activities.note: Shows what agent messages are FOR, in user tasks (notes, questions, approvals) rather than protocol language. Not a complete list — do not add "etc.".

ui.agentMessages.dialog.enable.tone: imperative verb, one word if the language allows
ui.agentMessages.dialog.enable.length: Button label; keep as short as possible.
ui.agentMessages.dialog.enable.note: The consent action: exactly one click enables agent messages for the signed-in account and tenant. The button stays disabled until a served consent is present.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.enabling.tone: ongoing, same verb stem as the idle label
ui.agentMessages.dialog.enabling.length: One short word plus ellipsis where the language styles progress that way.
ui.agentMessages.dialog.enabling.note: Shown while the enable request is in flight; all three dialog controls — Enable, Not now and the close X — are disabled in this state, so the dialog cannot be dismissed until the request settles. Do not change the verb from the idle "Enable" label beyond the grammar the language needs.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.not_now.note: Dismisses the dialog without enabling; the choice is remembered per account and tenant and the dialog does not return on its own. This button receives initial focus, so its label is read first by keyboard and screen-reader users.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.close.tone: single word, standard dialog close verb
ui.agentMessages.dialog.close.note: Accessible name only — the visible affordance is the X glyph. Behaves identically to "Not now": it dismisses and records the seen flag; mounting alone never enrolls.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.consent_unavaila.role: in-dialog standing when no consent text is served
ui.agentMessages.dialog.consent_unavaila.tone: calm, factual; states the negative outcome first
ui.agentMessages.dialog.consent_unavaila.length: One short sentence, may wrap to two lines.
ui.agentMessages.dialog.consent_unavaila.note: Shown where the served consent paragraph would be when the backend returns none. "Consent" is the product's term for the disclosure the user accepts; keep it consistent with Settings. Must not read like an error the user caused.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.account_guard_un.role: in-dialog refusal when the backend cannot bind consent to the account
ui.agentMessages.dialog.account_guard_un.tone: honest limitation, actionable next step, no internals
ui.agentMessages.dialog.account_guard_un.note: The account-guard refusal: this app/backend version cannot safely record consent against the signed-in account, so enabling is withheld. Names updating Local Operator as the fix. Do not name protocol mechanisms or raw error codes — the round-1 review asked for user guidance, not implementation detail.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.failure.tone: no blame, no cause speculation, give the retry path
ui.agentMessages.dialog.failure.note: Generic enable failure (e.g. the request was refused). It must not claim which side failed — offer "try again" and the Settings → Agent messages path. Never optimistic: the feature remains off.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.consent_changed.note: Shown when the served consent version changed under the user (409 consent_version_unknown); the dialog refreshed the consent text and requires a NEW explicit click. Say that the current text must be read and Enable pressed again — there is no silent retry, and this string is what explains the second click.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.local_failure.tone: reassuring about the saved consent, clear about the unfinished step
ui.agentMessages.dialog.local_failure.note: The consent write succeeded but this machine's setup did not finish. Must state the consent WAS saved so the user does not fear a lost choice, then point at Settings → Agent messages to finish. Distinct from the generic failure string.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.validation_failu.role: leading sentence for a rejected setup request
ui.agentMessages.dialog.validation_failu.note: Leads the validation-failure block; the technical {field}: {rule} line follows it as muted secondary detail. This sentence is what a non-technical user reads, so it must stand alone without the detail below it.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.validation_detai.role: muted secondary diagnostic under the validation-failure sentence
ui.agentMessages.dialog.validation_detai.tone: technical, unadorned, never the only explanation
ui.agentMessages.dialog.validation_detai.length: Compact; one identifier pair per line.

placeholders.field: Machine field name from the backend validation error (an identifier, e.g. a settings key). Keep verbatim — never translate.
placeholders.rule: Machine rule identifier from the backend validation error. Keep verbatim; do not expand into prose.

ui.agentMessages.dialog.validation_detai.note: Rendered only beneath the human guidance sentence (validation_failure), never instead of it. Design review round 1 required the plain sentence to lead and this pair to remain secondary.

ui.agentMessages.banner.title.length: One short line; the banner's first line.
ui.agentMessages.banner.title.note: The product name 'Team Bridge' stays in English in every language (a proper noun, like Radient). States the current fact: it is already on. It must not read as a question or an offer.

ui.agentMessages.banner.body.tone: plain, second person, no marketing claims
ui.agentMessages.banner.body.length: One or two sentences under the heading.
ui.agentMessages.banner.body.note: Says what the feature does and that nothing was sent when it turned on. 'Agent' follows the glossary. Never imply the reader still has to enable anything.

ui.agentMessages.banner.turn_off.length: One or two words; sits in a small button.
ui.agentMessages.banner.turn_off.note: Turns the feature off in one click. Same verb as the Settings Turn off action.

ui.agentMessages.banner.turning_off.note: Replaces the Turn off label while the request is in flight.

ui.agentMessages.banner.read.role: banner button that expands the consent text
ui.agentMessages.banner.read.length: Short phrase; a ghost button label.
ui.agentMessages.banner.read.note: Reveals the full consent text served by the hub. Phrase it as a path to understanding what the feature means, not as a legal acknowledgement.

ui.agentMessages.banner.hide.role: banner button that collapses the consent text
ui.agentMessages.banner.hide.note: Appears in place of the read label once the text is open.

ui.agentMessages.banner.dismiss.length: One or two words; never visible as text.
ui.agentMessages.banner.dismiss.note: Screen-reader name of the X that dismisses the banner for good. 'Dismiss' not 'Close': the banner does not come back.

ui.agentMessages.banner.consent_unavaila.note: Shown inside the expanded area only when the hub served no consent text. Not an error: nothing was lost.

ui.agentMessages.banner.turn_off_failed.note: Says the turn-off failed and that nothing was changed, then invites a retry. Do not say 'error' or blame the reader.

ui.agentMessages.banner.dismiss_failed.length: One short sentence plus a retry cue.
ui.agentMessages.banner.dismiss_failed.note: The notice stays visible after this failure.

ui.agentMessages.banner.turn_off_hint.role: banner helper text beside the Turn off button
ui.agentMessages.banner.turn_off_hint.length: One sentence; wraps under the buttons at narrow widths.
ui.agentMessages.banner.turn_off_hint.note: Says what Turn off takes away BEFORE the press: the Team Bridge page, conversations included, is hidden until the member turns it on again. Announced with the Turn off button. 'Team Bridge' is the product name; never translate it and never call it 'agent messages'.

ui.agentMessages.page_off.title.tone: sentence case, plain statement, product name kept as-is
ui.agentMessages.page_off.title.length: Short heading; one or two lines at a 512 px measure.
ui.agentMessages.page_off.title.note: Shown in place of the Team Bridge page after the member turned Team Bridge off themselves. States the state and its scope (this account, not the organization). 'Team Bridge' is the product name; never translate it and never call it 'agent messages'.

ui.agentMessages.page_off.body.tone: plain, calm, second person, no blame
ui.agentMessages.page_off.body.note: Says what being off means (no messages sent or received; conversations hidden, not deleted, until it is turned on again) and that turning it on again asks for consent. Sits above the button that opens Settings.

ui.agentMessages.page_off.action.length: Two to four words; sits in a small button.
ui.agentMessages.page_off.action.note: Opens Settings at the control that turns Team Bridge back on. It navigates; it does not turn anything on by itself. Avoid the word 'Enable'.
